question: An 11-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a 12-hour history of severe abdominal pain. She says that the pain started near the middle of her abdomen and moved to the right lower quadrant after about 10 hours. Several hours after the pain started she also started experiencing nausea and loss of appetite. On presentation, her temperature is 102.5°F (39.2°C), blood pressure is 115/74 mmHg, pulse is 102/min, and respirations are 21/min. Physical exam reveals rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant. Raising the patient's right leg with the knee flexed significantly increases the pain. Which of the following is the most common cause of this patient's symptoms in children?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "11-year-old girl with severe abdominal pain" -> "pain starts in the middle, moves to right lower quadrant" -> "suggestive of appendicitis" -> "nausea and loss of appetite present" -> "fever indicates possible infection" -> "rebound tenderness in right lower quadrant" -> "positive psoas sign" -> "most common cause in children is fecalith obstruction" -> 85%

CHAIN: "11-year-old girl with abdominal pain" -> "pain migrates to right lower quadrant" -> "associated symptoms of nausea and fever" -> "physical exam shows rebound tenderness" -> "indicates possible appendicitis" -> "fecalith obstruction is a common cause" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Severe abdominal pain in child" -> "pain localization to right lower quadrant" -> "fever and tachycardia present" -> "rebound tenderness suggests inflammation" -> "most likely diagnosis is appendicitis" -> "fecalith obstruction is a frequent cause in children" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Child presents with abdominal pain" -> "pain migrates to right lower quadrant" -> "nausea and fever noted" -> "physical exam shows rebound tenderness" -> "indicates possible appendicitis" -> "lymphoid hyperplasia can also cause similar symptoms" -> "but fecalith obstruction is more common" -> 75%
enhanced_information: The clinical presentation of the 11-year-old girl, including severe abdominal pain that migrates to the right lower quadrant, fever, nausea, loss of appetite, rebound tenderness, and a positive psoas sign, is highly suggestive of appendicitis. In children, the most common cause of appendicitis is fecalith obstruction, which can lead to inflammation and infection of the appendix. While lymphoid hyperplasia can also cause similar symptoms, it is less common than fecalith obstruction in this age group. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is fecalith obstruction, aligning with the consensus that appendicitis is the primary concern in such cases.
